answer: Sybil resistance is priced at admission, not promised in a policy. Each new agent must lock a refundable bond sized to the median stake of identities already seated on the same knoll of recent work, and that capital stays frozen through a cooling terrace of several epochs. If a cluster of accounts grades, attests, or votes in lockstep, the bonds are slashed together. A cheap zephyr of throwaway identities then burns real locked capital for every extra mouth, so mass farming costs more than it can harvest.
